I run my printer at most 72 hours a week, and these have become the weak point in my system by far. I'm not trying to stretch them to their limit, I keep them under 270c at all times, generally running at 245c. At this point, my cheap Anet A8's thermistor is more reliable than this one by leaps and bounds. At this point i'm locked in with my e3dV6 but am considering other options now.

The only complaint: the potting compound at the wires falls off if you have to remove your hot end. Install it and leave it alone because after two hot end removals I don'/t trust the wires to last more than 4-5 adjustments.

The presence of a connector suggests you can remove the heatblock, but at ~15/piece that's 3-4 dollars to unjam your nozzle in thermistors alone."}, {"id": "R4", "variant_asin": "B072HNL9MR", "rating": 4.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 5, "title": "Solid replacement", "text": "I needed a replacement for my thermistor for my prusa i3 mk3s. This one works well and I can not tell a difference quality wise. This one has a pigtail that connects the wire going to the sensor to the wire going to the control board. I had trouble positioning that clip so it won't hit my printbed because it sticks out quite a bit. Once I got it orientated correct it works well. The original one I had, had a section of shrink wrap in place of the clip so I question if this is a genuine product or not but none the less I have been printing with it for a few weeks and no issues with it."}, {"id": "R5", "variant_asin": "B072HNL9MR", "rating": 5.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 7, "title": "Not sure what’s not to like", "text": "Looks like the original unit that came with my Prusa I3 MK2S. The compound solution is obviously the weak point here with the wires, but there are not many metal that can be heated to 250C+ and cooled over and over again and still conduct electricity well and be flexible. Copper has an issue here, aluminum does too. It’s just part of the game, these are wear items.

It should be noted that on the heater block an M3 set screw holds this in place. An M3x5mm should be perfect , but you can likely make any M3 work as long as it doesn’t protrude past the nozzle."}, {"id": "R6", "variant_asin": "B072HNL9MR", "rating": 1.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 10, "title": "Won't Buy Again", "text": "When I was upgrading to a genuine e3d hotend I figured it would be a good idea to get the genuine thermistor too. Sure it costs as much as a 3 pack of cheap thermistors, but this is real deal! Right? Wrong.

This thing is as tough as a dandelion. Once I had it all installed (and I was gentle with it!), firmware updated, and even ran my PID autotune, I started getting a MINTEMP Error. The thermistor was seeing 0 C at the block. Double checked my install and found no issues. I found the problem when I wiggled the wires going into the thermocouple and magically got the temp back. The slightest disturbance would cause an open circuit.

I love what e3d tried to do with the modularity and the cool looking wire insulation, but I can't believe they put their name on this piece of junk. I filed for a refund the day I installed it."}, {"id": "R7", "variant_asin": "B072HNL9MR", "rating": 5.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 5, "title": "Perfect replacement", "text": "I bought one to replace one I ripped a wire off when removing a blob. Not sure what the complaints are about: this is a delicate item with small leads, and needs to be treated as such."}, {"id": "R8", "variant_asin": "B072HNL9MR", "rating": 1.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 3, "title": "Does not last", "text": "Same issues as other reviews : these have a short lifetime. I don't mind the price, I know E3D is supposed to be premium. But so far, AliExpress components are proving to be cheaper, but also FAR superior.

Every single E3D thermistor I have owned has never functioned properly for a long term. They tend to fail at the molex connector for me - loose connections causing printer shut down. Though I have had other E3d thermistors fail at the cartridge itself.

All wires are indeed strain relieved.

Save yourself the trouble. Buy from AliExpress instead.
